# 7 Airbnb upsells that boost revenue without annoying guests


by


[Guesty Marketing Team](https://www.guesty.com/blog/author/guesty-marketing-team/)


|


October 8, 2026 Reading time: 6 minutes


Share


Share


If you leave money on the table because you fear annoying your guests, you are thinking about upsells the wrong way. Most hosts view extra fees as a quick way to earn a bad review. Treat upsells as a sales tactic and your guests will rebel, but treat them as a convenience upgrade and they will gladly pay.


The secret to profitable Airbnb upsells is offering the exact thing your guest needs at the exact moment they need it. Do it right to boost your[profit margins](https://www.guesty.com/blog/smarter-pricing-for-short-term-rentals/) and improve the guest trip. Get it wrong, and you look greedy. Here is how to build an upsell program that drives revenue while earning you five-star reviews.


**TL;DR**


- Early check-in and late checkout offer the highest return on minimal effort.
- Pre-arrival grocery stocking and mid-stay cleans attract long-term and high-end guests.
- Pitch offers based on the specific purpose of the trip.
- Never offer an upsell during a stressful moment of the guest journey.
- Guesty® is a vacation rental software that ties your guest communication, task management, and payment processing into one automated flow so your upsell revenue never breaks your cleaning schedule.


## Why do guests want upsells?


An upsell is any additional product or service offered beyond the base nightly rate. To succeed, you must shift your mindset.


Guests expect to pay for convenience at hotels, gladly swiping their cards for room service, spa packages, and late checkouts. Bring that exact mindset to your short-term rental. Guests travel to relax and will gladly pay for shortcuts that remove friction from their trip.


A poorly executed upsell feels like a hidden fee, while a well-executed upsell feels like premium hospitality. Keep your base rate competitive and let guests build their own experience from your menu of extras.


## 7 profitable Airbnb upsells to offer your guests


Start small by picking one or two services from this list, and master the delivery before expanding your offerings.


### 1. Early check-in and late checkout


This offers the highest return on investment with zero hard costs. Guests constantly ask for schedule flexibility, so sell it by setting a flat hourly rate for every extra hour a guest stays outside your standard window.


If a guest buys a 2 p.m. late checkout via a manual text message, your cleaner might still arrive unnotified at 11 a.m. and walk in on them packing. Avoid this entirely by[automatically syncing](https://www.guesty.com/features/automation-tools/) your calendar and cleaner schedule before offering this service.


Disclose any[exterior security cameras](https://www.guesty.com/blog/airbnb-camera-policy-for-hosts/) or smart locks in your listing description and house rules if you use them to monitor check-in and checkout times for compliance.


### 2. Mid-stay cleaning and linen refresh


This appeals heavily to families and remote workers booking for a week or longer. A full week in a rental generates trash, dirty floors, and used towels. Offer a quick vacuum, trash removal, and fresh linen drop-off halfway through the trip. Charge a premium over your standard cleaning fee, pay your cleaner their standard rate, and keep the difference.


### 3. Pre-arrival grocery stocking


Nobody wants to navigate an unfamiliar grocery store after a six-hour flight, so offer to fill the fridge before arrival. Partner with a local service or have your turnover team pick up a standard list of staples. Charge the actual cost of the groceries plus a flat service fee or a percentage markup. Place the items neatly in the fridge and pantry, adding a welcome note for a high-end touch.


### 4. Pet accommodation packages


Pet owners are accustomed to travel fees. Offer a premium package alongside your standard pet fee, including a high-quality pet bed, water bowls, dog waste bags, and locally made treats. You secure extra revenue while the specialized items stay at the property for the next pet owner.

### 5. Rental gear


Look closely at your location and property type. Beach towns demand chairs, umbrellas, and coolers, while mountain towns demand snowshoes, sleds, or hiking poles. Buy high-quality gear once and rent it out continuously. Store these items securely on the property in a locked shed or closet, providing the access codes only to paying guests.


### 6. Celebration bundles


Anniversaries, birthdays, and honeymoons drive a significant portion of leisure travel. Offer a romantic bundle supplying champagne, local chocolates, and fresh flowers before arrival. You capture money the guest already planned to spend at a local florist. Partner with local vendors to secure wholesale pricing and increase your margin.


### 7. Curated local experiences and tours


Connect your guests directly with local businesses by partnering with a private chef, a boat captain, a massage therapist, or a winery. Negotiate a referral commission for every guest you send their way. You build local goodwill and improve the guest trip, all while adding zero extra physical work to your daily operations.


## Pitch your offers without feeling pushy


Personalizing the offer is critical, as blasting a pet package pitch to a corporate traveler feels like spam. Use Guesty to collect and store detailed guest profiles from previous stays or booking inquiries. If you see a returning anniversary trip on the calendar, pitch the celebration bundle. Track the data and send relevant offers.


Timing matters even more than the offer itself. Do not pitch an early check-in right after the guest books a stay six months in advance, because they have no idea what their travel schedule looks like yet. Wait until three days before arrival, and offer the late checkout on the evening before departure. Hit them exactly when they feel the need.


Use the Upsell closer to automate this timing. This AI agent analyzes the reservation data and automatically offers upsells to guests at the ideal moment for conversion. You secure the extra revenue, skip the manual sales pitch, and avoid annoying your guests with badly timed messages.


## Manual upselling creates operational chaos


Selling the extra service is easy, but delivering it is hard. Texting back and forth across Airbnb, Booking.com, Vrbo, and Expedia creates a massive administrative mess. You miss messages, forget to charge the guest, and fail to notify your cleaning team.


Build an automated workflow instead.


Task Manual upselling Automated workflows


**Communication** Trading chaotic text messages across four different apps Delivering targeted offers through a single unified inbox


**Fulfillment** Relying on sticky notes and memory to tell the cleaner Dispatching real-time updates directly to your cleaning team


**Payment** Chasing guests on cash apps after the trip ends Processing secure payments instantly before delivering the service


Give guests control over their own experience by sending a link to a digital guest portal. They can browse your extra services on their phone, select a late checkout, and pay securely via credit card.


Centralize your daily operations with[task management](https://www.guesty.com/features/tasks-management/) . When a guest buys a late checkout, your cleaner receives an instant notification adjusting the turnover schedule. The guest gets their extra time, your cleaner avoids a wasted trip, and you collect the margin.


Running a profitable upsell program requires connecting your guest communication directly to your cleaning schedules and payment processor. A[vacation rental software](https://www.guesty.com/) like Guesty® keeps your messaging, your AI agents, and your task assignments in one workspace. You capture the extra revenue without generating any extra chaos for your operations team.
